column3: “as at other times” renders “as time on time,” and “to seek omens” renders “to meet omens (nehashim).”

“his discourse” renders “his mashal” (also in verses 15, 20–21 and 23); “the oracle” renders “ne’um (utterance),” and “whose eye is opened” renders a word (shetum) that may mean “closed,” so the meaning is uncertain (also in verse 15).
“valleys” renders “wadis,” and “aloes” renders a word of uncertain identity.
“shatter them with his arrows” renders “his arrows he will strike”; the meaning is uncertain.
“struck his hands together” renders “clapped his hands,” and “you have persisted in blessing them” renders an emphatic doubled verb.
“I would honor you greatly” renders an emphatic doubled verb.
“contrary to the command of” renders “to transgress the mouth of,” and “of my own accord” renders “from my own heart.”
“in the days to come” renders “at the end of the days.”
“the forehead” renders “the corners (pe’ot),” and “tear down” renders a verb whose meaning is uncertain; “the sons of Sheth” may mean “sons of tumult.”
“your nest” renders “qen,” a play on the name “Kenite.”
“except God has ordained it” renders a terse phrase, “from when God ordains it”; the meaning is uncertain.
“the coast of Kittim” renders “the hand of Kittim.”
